refinement.vendor_agnostic_engine: OPERATOR FRAMING 2026-07-22 (authoritative): Handshake is a model/vendor-agnostic engine that WRAPS whatever runs the model. The CLI/terminal transport exists only because Anthropic subscription plans block economical direct API use - it is a lane, not the architecture. The wrapper owns: sandboxing, tool-call gating/stopping (SC MT-011), hooks (SC MT-012), cron/scheduling (SC MT-013), and exposing Handshake API/primitives as governed tools (SC MT-014). Claude and GPT are the first two engines; open-source/other vendors follow. Vendor harness behaviors in the research basis were input, not target; per-lane specifics live only in adapters and classification-table data; no vendor names in schemas, policy vocabulary, or operator-facing surfaces. A future direct-API lane replaces a CLI lane without touching wrapper capabilities. Implementing sessions must treat any vendor-coupled shortcut outside a lane adapter as a defect.

product_model.handshake: One application spanning professional IDE/model-harness and creative-production workflows. Managed projects may be software products, crawls/indexes, datasets, CKC character work, ComfyUI/LoRA work, Tailor assets, Studio documents, prototypes or other typed work.
product_model.surrealdb: Sole main database for all Handshake-managed projects and product modules; canonical mutations and EventLedger evidence remain Surreal-native.
product_model.managed_projects: A Surreal managed_project forest supports root projects, subprojects, task projects and prototypes. Every node owns a project-qualified Locus taskboard/WP/MT set. Workspaces are execution contexts linked to a project rather than project identity.
product_model.locus: Execution and work-tracking graph over managed projects, WPs, MTs, dependencies, claims, leases, gates and evidence. Parent rollups and filesystem/taskboard views are derived.
product_model.loom: Cross-domain graph, search, backlink and navigation substrate over typed references to Notes, code, media, datasets, CKC and future Tailor/Studio sources. Loom does not copy mutable source-module authority.
product_model.module_hierarchy: CKC is the product-navigation parent of future Tailor; Tailor keeps its tailor-domain and solver authority. Studio retains its current peer/top-level placement. Product-module hierarchy and managed-project hierarchy use different schemas and permission rules.

validation_plan: Real Surreal tests with repeated WP/MT IDs across nested and unrelated projects, authenticated record users, restart, hierarchy move, explicit cross-project dependency and denial paths.
Real Notes and CKC source entities produce one canonical project-scoped Loom projection; embed, backlink, search, delete, restore and repair use the source identity rather than synthetic blocks.
Loom graph/search plans are bounded and project-aware; inaccessible descendants do not leak through counts, facets, rank or diagnostics.
Turso loss/corruption/retry never changes Surreal truth; software and creative WP benchmarks drive a recorded ADOPT or REJECT verdict.

findings: Model-initiated spawn/steer is a privilege-escalation surface: mitigated by SwarmCoordinator-only spawn path, deny-by-default policy (MM MT-106), caps/leases, full ledger attribution, injection-scan (MM MT-104) on all inter-model content.
Upstream CLI contract drift (stream-json/app-server): mitigated by capability feature-detection, pinned version ranges, CI contract suites (CS MT-028, CX MT-047, AP MT-066), unknown-event tolerance.
Premature TS-editor removal: mitigated by machine-checked gate (TR MT-261) reading WP-012 evidence + PD MT-245 parity suite + operator sign-off row; gate RED today.
Annotation mis-attachment after edits: mitigated by multi-selector anchors, bounded fuzzy re-anchor, explicit ORPHANED/OUTDATED states, adversarial drift suite (AC MT-209).

Merge-back destroying work: mitigated by no-force invariant (grep-provable), no auto-conflict-resolution, protected-branch operator approval, abort-always-available, runtime negative proofs (WM MT-148).

Nested project identity collision or workspace/project aliasing can route one project's WP, MT, taskboard, lease or evidence into another; mitigated by typed project records, composite keys and authenticated denial proofs (MT-362..372).

Loom can accidentally become a second mutable authority for Notes or CKC; mitigated by one owning source record, typed projection registry, idempotent reconciliation and source-command routing (MT-381..398).
Project hierarchy and product-module hierarchy can be conflated; mitigated by separate relation schemas and CKC-to-Tailor navigation-only fixtures (MT-390..392).

Turso can become a hidden second database authority or lose work across a cross-database crash; mitigated by a narrow exception gate, strict allowlist, Surreal-first promotion proof and ADOPT/REJECT closure (MT-401..410).
minimum_controls: Every WP-017 behavior emits FR events + ledger rows fail-closed (RD MT-161/162).

SurrealDB remains the sole canonical authority; local databases, filesystem views and Loom source projections are bounded and repairable.
